cohort: The study included 402 preteens (9-11-year-olds) from the ROLO study, who were born to mothers that previously delivered an infant with macrosomia.
finding: Higher preteen physical activity was associated with lower sum of skinfolds and higher cardiorespiratory endurance, suggesting potential benefits for cardiometabolic health irrespective of birthweight, while early childhood physical activity and screen time were not related to preteen cardiometabolic outcomes.
birth_weight: Participants were born to mothers with a previous macrosomic delivery (birthweight >=4 kg); the study also investigated the interaction of the preteens' own birthweight.
